name: Under-eye filler (tear trough)

angle.text: Users have filler placed in the tear trough to soften hollowing and shadows that make the eyes look tired, with the effect visible right after treatment. It is widely used and fairly well described in reviews, in an area that calls for a skilled injector.

summary: Filler placed in the hollow under the eyes to soften shadowing; widely used and fairly well described, but a high-skill area where delayed swelling, lumps and rare vision-threatening events are documented.
note: Swelling after treatment is common; delayed lumps and rare orbital and vascular complications are reported in the literature.
currentQuick:
Tear trough filler is the injection of a soft gel, usually hyaluronic acid, into the groove between the lower eyelid and the cheek to reduce hollowing and dark shadows. It is used by clinicians as a non-surgical alternative to lower eyelid surgery.
On looksmaxxing forums it is mentioned as a small adjustment that can be noticeable in person without a plastic look. Medical literature describes it as common but technically demanding, with no standard evidence-based technique.
How it works: Filler placed in the tear trough camouflages the hollow and the bulge of orbital fat that creates a shadow, by adding volume under the skin [1]. HA was the most commonly reported product in delayed-complication cases, with poly-L-lactic acid and calcium hydroxylapatite also reported [2].
Risks and caveats: Swelling after infraorbital HA filler occurred in over half of patients in one retrospective review of 706 treatments, and was lower when a small amount of triamcinolone was mixed with the filler [4]. A systematic review of delayed complications identified swelling, lumps and xanthelasma-like reactions [2]. A first case of orbital compartment syndrome with retrobulbar haemorrhage after tear trough filler has been reported, managed without lasting visual loss [5].
deepLead:
Under-eye filler, or tear trough filler, is the injection of a dermal filler, most often hyaluronic acid (HA), into the tear trough, the depression running from the inner corner of the eye toward the cheek, to soften hollowing and shadowing under the eyes . Reviews state that dermal fillers can camouflage tear trough deformity and orbital fat pseudoherniation .
A systematic review of 42 articles on HA tear trough techniques found most evidence to be level III, with no standardized, evidence-based approach comparing needle and cannula injection . A case series of 198 eyes in 100 patients, mostly female, evaluated HA filler as an alternative to lower eyelid surgery .
Documented complications include post-injection swelling, delayed lumps and discoloration, and rare orbital events . Public interest in the procedure is visible in search data: Google Trends analysis found tear trough filler search interest changed by more than 50 percent within single weeks .

name: Liposuction / chin lipo

chain: Fat suctioned from chin and neck
angle.text: Users consider submental liposuction to remove fat under the chin and define the jawline and neck angle, since the fat cells removed do not return. Liposuction is common and well studied overall, with the neck-contour result visible once swelling settles.

summary: Surgical suction removal of fat, including under the chin and neck; common and well studied overall, with permanent fat-cell removal but contour irregularities and rare serious complications.
note: Surgery under anaesthesia: complications such as contour deformity, seroma and rarely deep vein thrombosis or embolism are documented.
currentQuick:
Liposuction removes localized fat using a thin suction tube (cannula) inserted through small incisions. In facial aesthetics it is used under the chin and along the neck to define the jawline and neck angle, sometimes combined with chin surgery.
On looksmaxxing forums it is sometimes described as a permanent way to keep the lower third lean, though others argue overall body fat can return. Reference sources say liposuction removes fat cells but that total body fat generally returns to its earlier level over months.
How it works: A cannula connected to suction is moved through the fat layer to remove cells, often after fluid containing dilute anaesthetic is injected (the tumescent technique) [11]. Removed fat cells do not regrow, but remaining fat cells can enlarge [11].
Risks and caveats: A 2024 meta-analysis of 39 studies and 29,368 patients found contour deformity (2.35 percent), hyperpigmentation (1.49 percent), seroma (0.65 percent) and haematoma (0.27 percent) among the complications [1]. Wikipedia notes rarer serious events, including deep vein thrombosis, organ perforation and embolism, and risk that rises with the volume removed [11].
deepLead:
Liposuction, also called lipoplasty or suction-assisted lipectomy, is a surgical procedure in which fat is removed from beneath the skin by suction through a cannula . Submental (chin) liposuction targets fat under the chin and along the neck, and in looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a way to define the jawline and neck angle.
Wikipedia reports that the technique was developed in Rome in the mid-1970s by Arpad and Giorgio Fischer, extended to the whole body by Yves-Gérard Illouz and Fournier, and that Jeffrey Klein's tumescent method using dilute lidocaine later enabled local-anaesthesia procedures . In the US it became the most commonly performed cosmetic procedure in 2015 according to the same source .
Reference sources say removed fat cells are permanently gone, but that overall body fat generally returns to its earlier level within months, with fat sometimes redistributing to other areas . A 2004 randomized study found that removal of subcutaneous fat by liposuction did not alter insulin action or coronary heart disease risk factors . The evidence base on submental liposuction specifically is limited to small registered studies and clinical practice.

name: Otoplasty (ear pinning)

chain: More balanced face from the front
angle.text: Users pin back protruding ears, and forum posters describe it as a low-cost add-on to jaw surgery that raises overall facial harmony. It is a long-established operation with high reported satisfaction, and the change in ear position is visible once healed.

summary: Surgery that sets protruding ears closer to the head; a long-established procedure with high reported satisfaction, usually discussed in looksmaxxing as a cheap add-on.
note: Evidence is mostly surgical case series and reviews; over 200 techniques exist and overcorrection or suture problems are documented.
currentQuick:
Otoplasty reshapes or repositions the cartilage of the outer ear. For prominent ears it is usually done by creating or restoring the fold of the antihelix, reducing a deep conchal bowl, or repositioning a protruding lobe. The aim is to bring the ear closer to the head.
In looksmaxxing forums it is often described as a high-return, relatively low-cost add-on, and some members say prominent ears can undermine otherwise balanced facial features. Reviews in the surgical literature describe high patient satisfaction, but note that no single technique is considered definitive.
How it works: Surgeons either use stitches that bend the cartilage into a fold without cutting it, score or cut the cartilage so it bends back, or remove a portion of the conchal cartilage. Some centres also describe closed, needle-based or minimally invasive versions. A head band is typically worn for several weeks afterwards to protect the shape.
Risks and caveats: Documented complications include hematoma, infection, suture extrusion, scarring, recurrence of prominence and overcorrection with an unnatural contour. A large case review of 562 patients reported significant morbidity including residual deformity. Forum members also discuss revision surgery for lobe or helix irregularities. Surgery is an Rx medical procedure performed by licensed surgeons.
deepLead:
Otoplasty, commonly called ear pinning, is plastic surgery of the outer ear (auricle). It is most often performed to correct prominent ears, sometimes called "bat ears", which result from an underdeveloped antihelical fold, an enlarged conchal bowl, or a protruding earlobe.  The same family of operations is also used for congenital malformations such as constricted ears, Stahl's deformity and cryptotia, and for ear reconstruction. 
Surgical reviews describe prominent ears as the most common abnormality of the external ear, and note that more than 200 different techniques have been described.  One 2005 review concluded there is no clearly definitive technique, while another noted that despite the variety patient satisfaction is generally high.  Evidence for otoplasty consists mainly of case series, retrospective comparisons and expert reviews rather than large controlled trials.
In looksmaxxing communities otoplasty is discussed as a small but visible surgical add-on, frequently mentioned alongside jaw surgery and rhinoplasty.  Members debate its payoff, its ideal timing and the risk of ending up with ears that look "pinned".

name: Gold thread lift

angle.text: Gold thread implantation is promoted for wrinkles and a lifting effect on the face. The evidence for that appearance use is a small clinical series, alongside a growing set of case reports describing retained threads.

summary: Implanting fine gold threads under the skin for wrinkles and 'lift'; documented mainly through a small clinical series and a growing set of case reports of retained threads.
note: Gold threads are permanent and radiopaque; case reports describe them appearing on X-rays years later and, in some cases, migrating or causing infection.
currentQuick:
Gold thread implantation places very fine strands of gold under the skin, historically in parts of Asia, in the hope of tightening skin, reducing wrinkles or relieving pain. Looksmaxxing discussion of it is sparse.
Published evidence is limited. One Korean-published series of 78 patients examined gold thread implantation for crow's feet. Most other literature consists of case reports describing threads found on X-rays or CT scans of patients who had the treatment years earlier.
How it works: Proponents of cosmetic gold thread therapy describe the threads as stimulating the skin or supporting tissue. A histopathology study examined skin that had gold threads implanted for facial rejuvenation. The exact mechanism for any lifting effect has not been established in the sources reviewed.
Risks and caveats: Case reports describe threads migrating, recurrent cellulitis, and incidental radiographic findings that can be mistaken for other conditions or obscure dental imaging. In one fatal case report, gold threads were found embedded at autopsy alongside electroacupuncture injuries; the report attributed the death to pneumothoraces after electroacupuncture, not to the threads themselves.
deepLead:
Gold thread implantation (also called gold thread therapy or gold thread acupuncture) involves inserting fine gold strands under the skin. Published reports describe it in cosmetic contexts such as facial wrinkles and rejuvenation, and in acupuncture-related contexts such as pain relief. 
The clinical literature is small. A series in Archives of Plastic Surgery evaluated gold thread implantation for periorbital wrinkles in 78 patients.  Much of the remaining literature consists of case reports and letters describing radiopaque threads found years later on chest, neck, jaw and spine imaging. 
The procedure is mentioned occasionally in looksmaxxing discussions as a 'lift' alternative to thread lifts, but community material is limited and no forum threads are cited here.

name: PDO thread lift

angle.text: Users choose PDO thread lifts as a minimally invasive way to lift sagging cheeks, jawline and neck tissue, with immediate improvement reported. PDO threads are the most commonly evaluated type in recent reviews, though long-term data are thin.

summary: Absorbable polydioxanone threads inserted under the skin to lift sagging tissue; immediate improvement is reported, but long-term data are thin.
note: Reviews describe mostly minor, short-lived adverse events but call long-term efficacy data lacking; practitioner training is unregulated in some countries.
currentQuick:
A PDO thread lift uses dissolvable polydioxanone sutures, sometimes with barbs or cones, placed beneath the skin to reposition or support sagging tissue in the midface, jowls or neck. It is performed in clinics without a surgical facelift incision.
In looksmaxxing circles it is discussed as a short-term way to get a sharper jawline or lifted cheeks. A 2025 systematic review found improvement on aesthetic scales immediately after treatment, while noting that previous studies had failed to show long-term efficacy for absorbable threads.
How it works: Threads are placed under the skin and anchored to tissue, mechanically suspending it. Absorbable materials such as PDO and poly-L-lactic acid dissolve over time, and a clinical study of PLLA/PLGA-containing threads found they stimulate collagen production in biopsies. Researchers differ on how much of any lasting effect comes from collagen stimulation versus mechanical lift.
Risks and caveats: Reviews describe mostly minor, self-limiting adverse events, such as bruising, swelling and asymmetry. A BBC investigation reported in Wikipedia found UK training courses with no mandatory qualifications and described poor infection control in an undercover recording; one physician quoted there called thread lifting the most dangerous aesthetic procedure because threads cannot be removed. PDO threads are medical devices administered by clinicians.
deepLead:
A thread lift is a minimally invasive procedure that uses sutures, often barbed or cogged, inserted under the skin to suspend ptotic (sagging) tissue. PDO (polydioxanone) threads are absorbable and are the most commonly evaluated thread in recent reviews. 
A 2025 systematic review of twelve studies covering 818 patients reported that aesthetic scores such as the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale and FACE-Q improved in all cases immediately after the procedure, while stating that previous studies had failed to show long-term efficacy for absorbable threads.  A 2017 review concluded that results with barbed sutures were inconclusive and that adverse events were mostly minor and short-lived. 
Thread lifts are marketed as a lower-downtime alternative to surgical facelifts. Forum discussion in looksmaxxing communities frames them as a temporary lift or jawline enhancer, though no forum threads are cited here.

name: Fox eye thread lift

angle.text: Popularised on social media and in aesthetic clinics, fox eye thread lifts use absorbable threads to raise the brow tail and outer eye for an upward tilt. Clinics report the lift is visible after treatment; no published study tests threads for this specific look.

summary: A cosmetic-clinic trend using threads to raise the outer brow and eye corner for an upward 'fox eye' tilt; no published study tests threads for this specific look.
note: Published work on 'fox eye' procedures is limited to a laser-protocol study and commentary; thread lifts in general have limited long-term data.
currentQuick:
The 'fox eye' look is an upward-slanting, elongated eye shape with a lifted outer corner and brow tail. The thread version uses absorbable threads, usually PDO, placed around the brow and temple region to pull tissue upward and outward in a clinic setting.
The term appears in cosmetic clinic marketing and on looksmaxxing forums, where related questions also include tape and canthoplasty. Academic literature on 'fox eye' procedures is sparse and no trial of threads specifically for this look was identified.
How it works: Thread lifts in general suspend soft tissue by anchoring absorbable sutures under the skin; the intended effect in this variant is elevation of the lateral brow and eye corner. A separate laser protocol named 'fox eyes lift' uses Er:YAG and Nd:YAG wavelengths, a different technique with the same goal.
Risks and caveats: Risks of thread lifts in general are discussed in reviews, which describe mostly minor and self-limiting events. Periorbital tissue is delicate, and surgical 'fox eye' procedures such as canthoplasty have been the subject of commentary and a study rating YouTube content on aesthetic canthoplasty as mostly poor quality and advertising-oriented.
deepLead:
'Fox eyes' refers to an eye appearance with an upward-angled outer corner and lifted brow tail, popularised through social media and aesthetic clinics. A 'fox eye thread lift' is a minimally invasive procedure that uses absorbable threads, commonly polydioxanone, to lift the brow and lateral eye region toward that shape. 
No published clinical trial testing threads specifically for the fox-eye aesthetic was identified. Related literature includes a split-face study of a laser protocol called the 'fox eyes lift' for eyebrow elevation, a letter about fox eye surgery, and a study of the quality of online canthoplasty videos. 
Within looksmaxxing communities 'fox eyes' are discussed as an attractive eye shape, with talk of surgery, threads and home methods such as taping.

name: Brazilian butt lift

angle.text: Users get a Brazilian butt lift to add glute volume and reshape the waist-to-hip silhouette using their own fat, and the change is visible once swelling settles. Surgical reviews document strong results, and some forum posters discuss male equivalents.

summary: Autologous fat transfer to the buttocks; powerful, well-documented results in surgical reviews, and a procedure with documented deaths that has driven safety changes.
note: Surgical literature reports deaths from gluteal lipoinjection; safety technique and anatomy are a central focus of the field.
currentQuick:
A Brazilian butt lift takes fat from elsewhere on the body by liposuction and injects it into the buttocks to add volume and reshape the silhouette. It is discussed in looksmaxxing forums mainly as a female-appearance procedure and as an analogue for male body contouring.
Surgical reviews describe gluteal fat grafting as the fastest growing body contouring operation, delivering results other procedures can not match, alongside a strong emphasis on safety and anatomy.
How it works: Fat is harvested, processed and injected into the buttock tissue. Some of the transferred fat is reabsorbed, so volume can change over the following months and repeat sessions are sometimes used. Ultrasound guidance is described by some surgeons as a way to visualise the injection plane.
Risks and caveats: Complications reported in the literature include fat resorption, asymmetry, infection, seroma and persistent numbness. A 2015 report from Mexican surgeons recorded 13 deaths from gluteal lipoinjection, and a 2019 meta-analysis reported complication rates of 7% for fat grafting versus 31% for implants. It is an Rx surgical procedure, and cosmetic tourism for it is a subject of media coverage.
deepLead:
Brazilian butt lift (BBL) is the common name for buttock augmentation using fat transfer, in which a patient's own fat is harvested by liposuction and injected into the gluteal region.  Wikipedia notes that the term probably comes from the Brazilian surgeon Ivo Pitanguy, who pioneered related surgery in the 1960s, while the Venezuelan surgeon Eduardo Krulig described buttock lipoinjection in 1987. 
Surgical reviews describe gluteal fat grafting as the fastest growing procedure in body contouring, and a large share of the recent literature focuses on safety, anatomy and technique.  A 2015 report documented deaths from gluteal lipoinjection among Mexican surgeons, and a 2019 meta-analysis put the complication rate for fat grafting at 7% against 31% for implants. 
In looksmaxxing forums the procedure is mostly discussed in terms of female appearance, with some users asking about male equivalents.

name: Facelift / neck lift

chain: Deeper tissues tightened and skin redraped
Younger, more defined jaw and neck
angle.text: Facelifts and neck lifts are used to tighten sagging tissue and give a more youthful, defined lower face and neck, with the change visible after healing. It is the most established anti-aging surgery, with decades of published techniques and complication data.

summary: Surgical lifting of the face and neck tissues; the most established anti-aging surgery, with decades of techniques and published complication data.
note: Hematoma and nerve injury are the main documented risks; reviews find no single technique clearly superior.
currentQuick:
A facelift (rhytidectomy) repositions and tightens facial tissues and usually removes excess skin to give a more youthful contour, and a neck lift addresses the jawline and neck, often by treating the platysma muscle. They are often combined.
In looksmaxxing forums, facelifts are discussed mainly as older-man anti-aging surgery and as a one-time investment, with arguments over whether to choose surgery or fillers. A review of facelift controversies concluded that the available techniques are generally equal in efficacy.
How it works: Techniques range from skin-only lifts to SMAS and deep plane lifts that reposition deeper layers, with neck work such as platysma plication or submental liposuction. Recent literature emphasises restoring volume and lifting vertically rather than pulling the skin sideways.
Risks and caveats: Documented complications include hematoma (the most common), nerve injury, skin necrosis (higher in smokers), scarring, hair loss at incisions and ear position changes. Wikipedia reports the ideal age for a facelift, by patient satisfaction, as 50 or younger, and cites typical skin-only results lasting 5 to 10 years.
deepLead:
A facelift, or rhytidectomy, is cosmetic surgery intended to give the face a more youthful appearance, typically by removing excess skin, tightening deeper tissues and redraping the skin of the face and neck. It is commonly combined with eyelid surgery and neck procedures. 
Facelift techniques have evolved through cutaneous, SMAS, deep plane and volumetric periods since the early 1900s.  A review of facelift controversies concluded that the literature suggests available techniques are generally equal in efficacy and called for higher-quality research with standardised outcome assessment. 
In looksmaxxing communities, facelifts and mini neck lifts are discussed by older men and by people who have lost weight, usually as complements to jaw surgery or fat grafting.

name: Fractional laser resurfacing

angle.text: Users turn to fractional laser resurfacing to smooth acne scars, texture, sun damage and uneven tone. It is well studied for scars and photoaging, with improvement building over weeks as the skin heals after a period of downtime.

summary: Clinic laser that treats skin in tiny columns to remodel scars and texture; well studied for scars and photoaging, with real downtime.
note: Ablative versions involve days of visible wounding and recovery; pigment and scarring complications are documented, especially in darker skin types.
currentQuick:
Fractional laser resurfacing uses a laser that treats a grid of microscopic columns of skin and leaves the tissue between them intact. It is offered by dermatologists and plastic surgeons for acne scars, other scars, wrinkles, sun damage and uneven texture.
In looksmaxxing communities it sits in the clinic-based 'hardmaxx' tier of skin treatment. Forum users describe it as a stronger option than at-home skincare, and some report that recovery is harder than expected.
How it works: Ablative lasers (such as CO2 and erbium) vaporize microscopic channels of skin, while non-ablative fractional lasers heat the tissue without removing it. The resulting controlled injury is described in the literature as stimulating new collagen and remodeling of the dermis. Because only a fraction of the surface is treated each time, healing is faster than with older fully ablative resurfacing.
Risks and caveats: Reported adverse effects include redness, swelling, crusting, acne flares, herpes simplex reactivation, pigment changes and scarring. Dermatology reviews describe skin phototyping (the Fitzpatrick scale) as relevant to predicting outcomes of procedures such as laser resurfacing. Treatments are performed by licensed clinicians; devices are regulated medical devices in most jurisdictions.
deepLead:
Fractional laser resurfacing is a cosmetic and medical procedure in which a laser delivers energy to the skin in a pattern of many microscopic zones, leaving untreated skin between them. It is used for scars (especially atrophic acne scars), wrinkles, sun-damaged skin, stretch marks and uneven texture, and is a form of the broader category of laser skin resurfacing. 
Fractional devices come in two main kinds. Ablative systems, typically CO2 or erbium lasers, vaporize tissue in the treated columns; non-ablative systems, such as the 1550 nm devices marketed as Fraxel, heat the dermis without removing the surface.  Fractional treatment was developed after earlier fully ablative CO2 resurfacing, which produced notable results but also high complication rates. 
Clinical studies, consensus reports and randomized trials support fractional laser treatment for several scar types, with improvement typically gradual over multiple sessions. Reported adverse effects include prolonged redness, pigment changes, infection and scarring, and downtime for ablative treatments is several days.  Forum users on looksmax.org discuss it as a clinic option within skin-focused looksmaxxing and describe heavy downtime.

name: Professional microneedling / RF microneedling

angle.text: Users get clinic microneedling, sometimes with radiofrequency, to improve acne scars, texture and fine lines. A moderate body of trials supports scar and texture use, while claims about denser beard, eyebrow or scalp hair are less well studied.

summary: Clinic collagen-induction treatment using fine needles, sometimes with radiofrequency; a moderate body of trials for scars and texture, weaker for hair and add-ons.
note: Evidence is strongest for acne scars and skin texture; PRP and exosome add-ons and hair-growth claims rest on smaller or mixed studies, and non-clinical 'vampire facial' settings have been linked to infection outbreaks.
currentQuick:
Professional microneedling uses a device with many fine needles to make controlled punctures in the skin. RF microneedling adds radiofrequency energy delivered through the needles. Clinics offer it for acne scars, fine lines, skin laxity and texture.
In looksmaxxing forums it is often compared with at-home dermarolling, and some users recommend clinic RF treatment over deeper home needling. Reviewers in dermatology describe it as minimally invasive with a broad range of uses.
How it works: The needles create small channels and a wound-healing response that is described as stimulating collagen and elastin production. RF versions heat the dermis around the needle tips. Clinics sometimes apply serums, platelet-rich plasma or other products to the skin during the procedure.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include redness, swelling and pinpoint bleeding after treatment, with infection and scarring possible. In 2024 the US CDC reported HIV infections linked to a spa offering PRP microneedling facials, which prompted health-department warnings about non-clinical settings. Devices and sterile technique matter; treatment should be done by licensed clinicians.
deepLead:
Microneedling, also called collagen induction therapy or skin needling, is a cosmetic procedure in which fine needles repeatedly puncture the skin to trigger a healing response. Professional versions use motorized pens with adjustable needle depth, and radiofrequency (RF) microneedling adds energy delivered through the needles to heat the deeper skin. 
Reviews list applications including acne scars, rhytides, surgical scars, pigment disorders, enlarged pores, stretch marks and transdermal delivery of topical drugs, and describe the technique as minimally invasive.  Trials have tested it for acne scars, melasma, skin laxity, hair loss and combined with platelet-rich plasma or exosomes. 
The evidence is mixed by indication: systematic reviews report microneedling as efficacious in melasma but not clearly better than the standard topical hydroquinone, and a review found evidence for adding PRP to microneedling for acne scars less supportive than for PRP with fractional laser.  On looksmax.org, users discuss at-home dermarolling at length, while some recommend dermatology-office RF microneedling for deeper work.

name: Medical tourism (Turkey/Istanbul/Korea)

angle.text: Looksmaxxers travel to Turkey or South Korea for cosmetic surgery, hair transplants and dental work at lower prices than at home, often combining procedures in one trip. It is a way of accessing other procedures rather than an appearance change itself; reviews discuss infection and follow-up care.

summary: Travelling abroad, often to Turkey or South Korea, for cosmetic surgery, hair transplants or dental work at lower prices; reviews flag infection and follow-up-care risks.
note: Published literature on medical tourism documents infectious complications, limited aftercare and insurance gaps; outcomes vary widely by clinic.
currentQuick:
Medical tourism means travelling to another country to obtain non-emergency medical care. In appearance culture the term usually refers to surgery, hair transplants and dental work in places such as Istanbul, Antalya or South Korea, where prices can be lower than in the patient's home country.
There are no controlled trials of 'looksmaxxing trips' as such. Public-health reviews of medical tourism in general describe benefits such as access and cost, alongside complications and continuity-of-care problems.
How it works: Patients usually book through clinics or agents, travel for a package that can include surgery, accommodation and transfers, and return home within days to weeks. Follow-up care after return is arranged with local clinicians, if at all.
Risks and caveats: Reviews report infections (including outbreaks of fungal meningitis linked to cosmetic surgery in Mexico), difficulty arranging follow-up, and possible clotting risks with long flights after surgery. Legal recourse and insurance coverage for complications can be limited. Regulation differs by country; Turkey introduced a regulation on international health tourism in 2017.
deepLead:
Medical tourism is travel abroad to obtain medical treatment. Historically it meant patients from poorer countries seeking care in wealthy ones; more recently it often means patients from high-income countries travelling to lower-cost destinations, usually for surgery, dental work or fertility treatment, with cosmetic surgery a large category. 
In appearance-focused communities, Turkey (especially Istanbul and Antalya) is known for hair transplants and dental veneers and crowns, and South Korea for facial cosmetic surgery.  A 2024 ISAPS analysis of global aesthetic statistics reported 34.9 million surgical and nonsurgical aesthetic procedures by plastic surgeons in 2023 and included questions on the prevalence of medical tourism. 
Academic reviews note that medical tourism is growing and that infectious complications and continuity of care are recurring concerns.  The evidence base consists mainly of reviews, case series and scoping studies rather than trials.

name: Gastric sleeve

angle.text: Gastric sleeve surgery is discussed as a route to substantial fat loss, which users link to a leaner face and body. It is well studied for weight loss and diabetes in severe obesity, with documented surgical and nutritional risks.

summary: Bariatric operation that removes most of the stomach; well studied for weight loss and diabetes, with documented surgical and nutritional risks.
note: Medical surgery for obesity, not a cosmetic procedure; irreversible, with leak, reflux, deficiency and weight-regain risks.
currentQuick:
Sleeve gastrectomy is a surgery in which most of the stomach is removed, leaving a narrow tube. It is a mainstream medical treatment for obesity and is the most commonly performed bariatric operation worldwide, according to Wikipedia.
Its evidence base is large because it is studied as a medical treatment rather than a cosmetic one; it is listed in this wiki because large weight loss changes body and facial appearance.
How it works: Removing roughly three quarters or more of the stomach along its outer curve limits how much food can be eaten and removes the part that produces the appetite hormone ghrelin. Research also describes broader effects on gut hormones and glucose handling that are not fully explained by weight loss alone.
Risks and caveats: Documented risks include staple-line leaks, bleeding, clots, infection, reflux, nausea and vomiting, vitamin and thiamine deficiencies (including rare Wernicke encephalopathy), gastric dilation, and weight regain that may lead to revision surgery. The operation is considered irreversible. Eligibility is set by clinical guidelines based on body mass index and health conditions.
deepLead:
Sleeve gastrectomy, often called the gastric sleeve, is a bariatric operation usually performed laparoscopically in which a large portion of the stomach is removed along its greater curvature, leaving a narrow tube-shaped stomach.  It is used to treat severe obesity and obesity-related conditions such as type 2 diabetes. 
Wikipedia describes it as having begun as a modification of the duodenal switch and as the first stage of a two-step operation in very high-risk patients before being used on its own, and as now the most commonly performed bariatric surgery worldwide.  Systematic reviews report weight loss and comorbidity resolution comparable to gastric bypass, along with risks such as staple-line leak. 
The sources reviewed here concern the sleeve as a medical obesity treatment rather than a cosmetic one; its weight loss can change body and facial appearance, but no studies on appearance outcomes specifically were identified.

name: Veneers / Turkey teeth

angle.text: Users get porcelain or composite veneers for a uniform, brighter smile, and 'Turkey teeth' refers to cheap multi-tooth makeovers from Turkish clinics. The change in colour and shape is visible straight away, and veneers are durable in studies.

summary: Thin ceramic or composite shells bonded over teeth for a uniform smile; durable in studies, but preparation can remove enamel and the cheap multi-tooth 'Turkey teeth' packages draw scrutiny.
note: Prepared teeth cannot regrow enamel; outcomes depend on how much tooth is removed and on bonding technique.
currentQuick:
Veneers are thin shells of porcelain or composite resin bonded to the front of teeth to change colour, shape or apparent alignment. Wikipedia notes they are sometimes nicknamed 'Turkey teeth' in reference to dental tourism, and 'Hollywood smile' is the name for multi-tooth makeovers.
Systematic reviews of ceramic laminate veneers report high survival rates over about a decade. In looksmaxxing forums, veneers are discussed as a way to improve the smile and sometimes as a stand-in for orthodontics, including on trips to Turkey.
How it works: The dentist usually removes a thin layer of enamel (the amount varies, and some systems use little or none), takes an impression or digital scan, and bonds a veneer made in a lab or chairside. Reviews stress that bonding to enamel, rather than exposed dentin, and proper surface treatment of the ceramic are linked to better outcomes.
Risks and caveats: Reported complications include chipping, debonding, marginal staining, sensitivity and decay. Preparation that exposes dentin is associated with lower success rates, and the loss of enamel is not reversible. Critics cited by Wikipedia describe overuse of veneers on healthy teeth as 'instant orthodontics'.
deepLead:
A dental veneer is a layer of material, most often dental porcelain or composite resin, bonded to the front surface of a tooth to change its colour, shape, size or apparent position.  Laminate veneers are mostly cosmetic and cover only the facial surface, while full veneer crowns cover all coronal surfaces.  Multi-tooth cosmetic makeovers are commonly called 'Hollywood smile' treatments, and the term 'Turkey teeth' has become a nickname for veneers or crowns obtained cheaply at dental clinics in Turkey. 
The clinical literature on ceramic laminate veneers is substantial. A 2025 systematic review and meta-analysis of 29 studies reported pooled survival of about 96% for feldspathic, 94% for leucite-reinforced and 97% for lithium disilicate veneers at around 10 years, with technical complications more frequent for feldspathic ceramics.  A 2024 narrative review similarly found satisfactory survival and success for these ceramics, with dentin exposure lowering success. 
In looksmaxxing communities veneers are described as a high-impact change to facial appearance, and posters discuss dental work as part of surgery trips to Turkey.  The research literature covers the clinical performance of veneers; no studies were identified on the 'Turkey teeth' practice as a defined phenomenon.

name: Calf implants

angle.text: Users with thin calves or stubborn calf size consider silicone implants to add lower-leg volume, and bodybuilders seek them for size. The added volume is visible after healing, and evidence comes from surgical case series.

summary: Silicone implants placed in the lower leg to add calf volume; documented in surgical case series with notable complications such as compartment syndrome.
note: Evidence is surgeon-reported case series and literature reviews, not controlled trials; rare but serious complications such as compartment syndrome are reported.
currentQuick:

Eye color change surgery refers to procedures intended to alter the apparent color of healthy eyes. Bonesmashing (also bone smashing or face hammering) is a looksmaxxing practice in which people strike their own facial bones, typically with a hammer or similar object, in the belief that the resulting trauma will remodel the bone into a more defined, "chiselled" shape . It belongs to the bonehacks category of looksmaxxing.

It has nonetheless drawn attention from journalists and surgeons: letters in oral and maxillofacial surgery journals in 2024 described it as a dangerous trend spread on TikTok , and a 2026 cross-sectional study of social-media discourse recorded thousands of mentions of the term . No clinical study has tested whether it changes facial structure.
